name: inprocess-obi-apb-wb-tlul-mixed-timer-uart-rvtimer-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches three independently addressed MMIO targets of three different protocols in one process, with no AXI4-Lite target: the PULP timer at 0x40001000 (APB3, the one F5 target), the ZipCPU UART at 0x40002000 (Wishbone classic) and the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000 (TL-UL). This session states the three protocols' words without an AXI4-Lite group, so the neutral counter group is the Wishbone one and the TL-UL group prints its own tlul_error word.
notes: An APB3 + Wishbone + TL-UL session with no AXI4-Lite target: target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000 behind the real apb3_mmio_bridge (apb/3), target 1 is the ZipCPU UART at 0x40002000 behind the real beat_to_wishbone adapter (wishbone/classic, word-addressed registered-ack), target 2 is the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter (tl-ul/1).
The three windows are disjoint (0x40001000..0x40002000, 0x40002000..0x40002010, 0x40003000..0x40004000), none overlaps the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000, and all clear the 4 GiB bound.
Registers: TIMER0_COUNT(0)/TIMER0_CTRL(4)/TIMER0_CMP(8) on the APB3 timer; SETUP(0)/FIFO_STATUS(4)/RXREG(8)/TXREG(12) on the Wishbone UART; CTRL(0x4)/COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118) on the TL-UL rv_timer.

Only target 0 declares F5 facts, through configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json, so F5 remains the APB3 timer's own window and the other two targets are reached by F2/F4 only. The summary states target1_f5 no and target2_f5 no.

This session is the no-AXI4-Lite three-protocol case: the case line prints the neutral counter group once (the Wishbone group prints target_transfers and target_error), the TL-UL group prints its own tlul_a_handshakes/tlul_d_handshakes/tlul_errors and a tlul_error word, and no axi_* group exists because the build has no AXI4-Lite target.
No DMA is declared; the route criterion is the APB3 one and no route is claimed. F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB3+Wishbone+TL-UL.
The three profiles declare 50 MHz each, so one host tick drives all four models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.
